first_record.differential_diagnosis: 1. Meniere's disease: More common in young females, acute onset, characterized by recurrent vertigo, fluctuating tinnitus, and hearing loss. The more frequent the attacks, the longer and more severe the vertigo. This patient has no history of similar episodes, and current symptoms do not support this. 2. Vestibular neuritis: Etiology unclear, mostly viral, affecting peripheral vestibular organs/neurons. Common in 30-50yo, sudden onset, often preceded by fever/URI. Severe vertigo exacerbated by head movement, peaking in hours to days, gradually improving. Usually no tinnitus/deafness. Spontaneous nystagmus present initially. This patient had no prodromal fever, and combined with history and dizziness characteristics, this is basically excluded.
first_record.plan: 1. Neurology routine nursing, Level II care, low-salt/low-fat/diabetic diet; 2. Low VTE risk, complete admission workup to guide further management. 3. Administer neurotrophic and microcirculation-improving therapy; 4. Consult attending physician for guidance. The preliminary diagnosis and plan were explained to the patient/family, who understood and agreed.
